short_summary: HealthRate, a Minneapolis-based SaaS platform for comparing high-cost medical case rates, announced integration of SRTR quality data to let users evaluate transplant providers by cost and quality.
long_summary: HealthRate, an award‑winning SaaS application headquartered in Minneapolis, MN, specializes in comparing network‑contracted rates for high‑cost medical cases such as transplants, CAR‑T, and gene therapy. The company announced that it has integrated Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) quality data into its platform, allowing users to assess transplant providers on both cost savings and gold‑standard quality metrics. This integration addresses the problem of lacking combined cost and quality data for transplant provider evaluation. Tim Michaels, CEO of HealthRate, emphasized that the new data empowers payers, providers, and patients to make value‑driven decisions. Target customers include payers, providers, and patients.

## What is SRTR?

The Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) is a federally funded database that collects, analyzes, and publicly reports on the performance of all solid organ transplant programs and organ procurement organizations in theUnited States. Operating under contract with the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) and in coordination with the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN), SRTR is recognized as the gold standard for transplant quality metrics due to its comprehensive, independent, and publicly accessible data.
